chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abbas ibn Amir, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who intends to perform Hajj: should he trim his hair throughout the entire month of Shawwal, provided he has not seen the crescent (of Dhu al-Qidrah)? He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (title of Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْهِلَال: The crescent moon (marking the beginning of a lunar month)
key_terms.شَوَّال: Shawwal (the 10th month of the Islamic calendar)

ai.seo_question: When can a pilgrim trim their hair before entering the state of Ihram for Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the temporal boundary for the prohibition of hair trimming for those intending Hajj, ruling that the restriction begins only upon the sighting of the Dhu al-Qidmah crescent. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that the state of Ihram obligations are contingent on the specific lunar markers rather than a fixed calendar date, allowing flexibility in Shawwal for preparatory grooming.
